[[Long Lake, Minnesota]] | tournaments = Y | tournament_list = * 4x Big 10 ([[2008 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2008]], [[2009 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2009]], [[2010 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2010]] & [[2011 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2011]]) * 4x NCAA ([[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008]], [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009]], [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010]] & [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011]]) * [[Maui Invitational]] (2009) * [[Old Spice Classic]] (2010) | championships = Y | championship_list = * [[Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament]] ([[2008 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2008]]) }} '''Jon Leuer''' (born May 14, 1989 in [[Long Lake, Minnesota]]) is a [[college basketball]] player for the [[Wisconsin Badgers]].http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1985852 He has been a two year starter and enters the 2010-2011 season on the [[Wooden Award]] preseason watch list and is on the preseason All-[[Big Ten]] first team.{{cite web|title=UW men's basketball: Leuer named to preseason all-Big Ten team|url=http://iplextra.indiatimes.com/article/03F57544xPgd6?q=Michigan|publisher=Madison.com|accessdate=30 October 2010}}http://ncaabasketball.fanhouse.com/2010/10/04/wooden-award-preseason-2010-11-watch-list/ [[SI.com]] named Leuer their 2010-11 Big Ten preseason player of the year.http://host.madison.com/sports/blog/article_1be58e48-e773-11df-8c69-001cc4c03286.html ==High school== Leuer attended [[Orono_school_district#Orono_High_School|Orono High School]] in [[Long Lake, Minnesota]] and was ranked the 82nd best [[college]] recruit in the [[nation]] from the class of 2007.http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-1611 One scouting report read: "At 6-foot-10, 200-pounds, Leuer definitely needs some time to fill out his frame for high-major competition. Nonetheless, he is a pure shooter with good overall skills with the ball. He can knock down a jump hook and can play off the dribble. He moves well up and down the court, but has a ways to go defensively and as a rebounder. Could be an impact player with his size and unique skill set if he does get stronger."http://rivals.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Jon-Leuer-52068;_ylt=Ajd.cPsdVI8RuNM32I6SwiLVO5B4 Another one stated: "Flew under the radar prior to the spring of 2006. Excellent player from behind the stripe, especially when you consider that he pushes 6-10. Face up four man will need to add strength to reach his potential. Could be an [[Andrew Brackman]] type of forward."http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1985852 His [[junior year]] he averaged 18 points and 8 [[rebounds]] per game and earned honorable mention all-state and first-team all-conference honors. He averaged 23.2 points and 12.0 rebounds per game as a senior and was selected to [[Minnesota]] State [[All-star game]] while landing second-team all-state and first-team all-conference honors.http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leuer_jon00.html He ended up with 35 double digit scoring games and a career high of 37.http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leuer_jon00.html He played [[AAU basketball]] with the Minnesota Magic. The Magic has a list of distinguished [[NBA]] [[alumni]] including [[Khalid El-Amin]], [[Troy Bell]], [[Kris Humphries]], [[Cole Aldrich]] and [[Joel Pryzbilla]]. Among the current [[college]] stars who played with the Magic are [[Blake Hoffarber]] from the [[University of Minnesota]], P.J. Hill from [[Ohio State]], and Leuer's [[University of Wisconsin]] teammate, Jordan Taylor.http://www.magicbasketball.org/magic_alumni.htm Leuer had originally entered high school as a [[Guard (basketball)|guard]], but had a 10 inch [[growth spurt]] before his [[senior year]].http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leuer_jon00.html ==College== '''Freshman season''' Leuer never started, but played in 32 games during the 2007-2008 season. The most points he scored during the non-conference season was 12, but he exploded for 25 (on 8 of 9 shooting) against the [[Michigan Wolverines]] in the [[Big Ten]] opener. However, after scoring 7 in the follow-up game, Leuer would only score 9 points for the remainder of the season.http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Leuer&action=submit Much of this spoke to Wisconsin's great depth, as the Badgers would go on to win both the [[Big Ten]] regular season, with a 16-2 record, and [[Big Ten Conference Tournament]]. They would later advance to the [[Sweet Sixteen]] in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] and finished with a 31-5 record.http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-2007-08-sched.html Leuer finished the season averaging 2.9 points per game and 1.3 rebounds in 8.6 minutes. '''Sophomore season''' Leuer played in all 33 games and started the final 12 games of the year during the 2008-2009 season. He had 13 double digit scoring games including 17 in a [[victory]] at [[Virginia Tech]] in the [[ACC-Big Ten Challenge]]. He had a season high of 19 points against [[SIU-Edwardsville]]. He averaged 8.8 points per game and 3.8 rebounds in 21.3 minutes. The Badgers finished tied for fourth in the [[Big Ten]] with a 10-8 record, and a 20-13 record overall.http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=36138&year=2009 They would upset the #5 seeded [[Florida State Seminoles]] in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] before succumbing to the [[Xavier Musketeers]] in the second round.http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-2008-09-sched.html Leuer was named to the [[Academic]] All-Big Ten Team.http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leuer_jon00.html '''Junior season''' The Badgers went into the 2009-2010 season picked 9th in the [[Big Ten]]. However, they upset the [[Arizona Wildcats]] and [[Maryland Terrapins]] in the [[Maui Invitational]].http://www.mauiinvitational.com/index.asp# On December 2, 2009, in a game on [[ESPN]], Wisconsin shocked the #5 [[Duke Blue Devils]] (who would be the eventual National Champions).http://webcache.googleusercontent.com/search?q=cache:pm5yuPyvMm8J:badgerherald.com/news/2009/12/03/badgers_shock_duke_a.php+2009+badgers+picked+ninth+basketball&cd=3&hl=en&ct=clnk&gl=us&client=firefox-a Leuer poured in 17 points on his way to scoring double digits in 13 of the first 15 games of the year. He followed up the effort against Duke with back-to-back double doubles at [[UW-Green Bay]] (a career high 26 points and 10 rebounds) and against [[Marquette University]] (24 points, 12 rebounds). He would also score 25 against [[UW-Milwaukee]] and 21 at [[Michigan State]].http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=36138&year=2010 Wisconsin was off to a surprising 13-3 start (3-1 in the [[Big Ten]]) after a 73-66 upset against #4 [[Purdue]]. However, Leuer had an off night against [[Purdue]] and only scored 4 points on 2-15 shooting. It was revealed after the game that Leuer had broken his [[wrist]] in the first half, yet still played 38 of the 40 minutes in the game. Leuer was ruled out indefinitely and he ended up missing the next 9 games.{{cite web|title=Badgers lose Leuer with broken wrist|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=4816123|publisher=[[ESPN]]|accessdate=30 October 2010}} When Leuer returned, he was eased back into the lineup, scoring 4 points in his first game back, a loss against the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. However, Leuer would score double digits in each of the final five games of the year, including 20 against the [[University of Illinois]], as the Badgers went 4-1 down the stretch and finished 13-5 in the [[Big Ten]], good enough for fourth place and a #13 national ranking. Leuer won [[Big Ten]] Player of the week for the final week of the regular season. Yet, the Badgers would lose to the [[Illinois Fighting Illini]] in the first round of the [[Big Ten Tournament]] and were upset by [[Cornell]] in the second round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]], despite 14 and 23 points from Leuer respectively.http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-sched-2009.html Leuer ended up leading the Badgers in points per game (15.4),rebounds per game (5.8), and blocks per game (1.33). Due to the wrist injury, he only played in 24 games, starting 22 of them. His .522 [[field-goal percentage]] was the highest by a Wisconsin player since [[Alando Tucker]]'s .533 mark in 2003. He earned honorable mention All-[[Big Ten]], despite missing half of the conference games. He also made the [[Academic]] All-[[Big Ten]] team for the second straight year.http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leuer_jon00.html '''Summer of 2010''' During the summer, Leuer was selected to be on the [[USA]] men's select team, a team of [[college]] players hand-picked to help the [[United States men's national basketball team]] prepare for the [[FIBA World Championships]]. Leuer went with the team to [[New York City]] to compete against the likes of [[Kobe Bryant]], [[Lebron James]], and [[Dwyane Wade]].http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_86cc4150-8aaa-11df-9820-001cc4c03286.html Leuer had been named to the team after impressing [[Team USA]], and [[Villanova]], [[coach (sport)|coach]], [[Jay Wright]]. When Gary Parrish of [[CBSSports.com]] asked Wright to name the best [[college]] player with the [[USA Basketball]] select team, Wright picked Leuer over [[Kyle Singler]], [[Nolan Smith]], [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus Morris]] and others.http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_29ed892c-9a49-11df-b22a-001cc4c03286.html “He’s really good,” Wright told Parrish. “Maybe I haven’t followed him as well because he’s from the [[Midwest]], and maybe he wouldn’t surprise anybody else. But he’s got great size, he puts it on the floor, he passes it, he can shoot it. He’s just a ballplayer.” When asked if he would be an [[NBA]] player, Wright answered "yes."http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_5754bc22-9e5f-11df-9ada-001cc4c002e0.html '''Senior season''' Leuer heads into his senior season as a preseason All-[[Big Ten]] selection and on the [[Wooden Award]] preseason watch list. He needs 245 points to join Wisconsin's 1,000 point club. He is ranked 10th in UW history with .492 career field-goal percentage. Wisconsin enters the season ranked #24 in the [[ESPN/USA Today Coaches' poll]] and just missing the top 25 in the [[Associated Press Poll]], accumulating the 26th most votes.http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings In both polls, the Badgers are the fifth ranked [[Big Ten]] team. [[SI.com]] named Leuer their Big Ten preseason player of the year. About Leuer, Luke Winn wrote: "Watch out for Leuer, an ultra-efficient, 6-foot-10 forward who'll be the Badgers' clear No. 1 offensive option for the first time in his career," Winn wrote in an article published Wednesday. "He drew rave reviews from USA Basketball coaches for his work on the college select team this summer -- especially for his mid-range moves and driving skills -- and could very well enjoy a 20-and-8 season as a senior, putting himself in the conversation to become a the first UW player drafted since Alando Tucker. "Leuer would be more of a household name already, had a broken left wrist not disrupted his promising junior year." On December 28, 2010 the Badgers upset theN #13 ranked [[Minnesota Golden Gophers]], 68-60. During the first half of the game, Leuer became the 36th player in Wisconsin Badgers history to score 1,000 points in a career. On March 1, 2011 Leuer was named to the [[Yahoo Sports]] All-Big Ten 1st team.http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news;_ylt=AiMYsNUhdGD6.szznqPvLwbevbYF?slug=jn-bigten030111 Yahoo Sports All-Big Ten Team Leuer is a finalist for the [[Lowe's Senior CLASS Award]]. He was picked to the Third Team All-America by [[Fox Sports]].{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711|title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams|work=[[Fox Sports]]||publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|date=Mar 7, 2011|accessdate=June 21, 2011}} Leuer was named to the [[Yahoo Sports]] All-American Team Honorable Mention.http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=jn-allam030711 Leuer Yahoo Sports Honorable Mention ==Personal== Jon is the son of Mike and Holly. He has two older sisters, Maren and Katie.
